name: Rosemary (ct. Cineole)
source_reference: ISO 1342:2012 - Oil of rosemary; Arctander, 'Perfume and Flavor Materials of Natural Origin', 1960
notes: The cineole chemotype is the most common commercial grade. The camphor chemotype (Spain) has camphor up to 25%. The verbenone chemotype (Corsica) is rarer and sweeter.

key_markers.470-82-6: 1,8-Cineole - defines the cineole chemotype, fresh eucalyptus-like
key_markers.76-22-2: Camphor - camphoraceous sharpness, must be moderate in cineole CT
key_markers.80-56-8: alpha-Pinene - piney freshness, second monoterpene after cineole

olfactive_description: Fresh, herbaceous-camphoraceous with clean eucalyptus-like top notes. Aromatic and stimulating with warm, slightly woody undertones. More complex and rounded than eucalyptus.
